source: NPTEL Week 2 assessment, Jul–Oct 2026 run (accepted answers, reworded)

questions.question: Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) is used for:
options: Propagating gradients back across the time steps of a sequence
questions.explanation: The RNN is unrolled over time and gradients flow back through every step.

questions.question: The hidden state of an RNN mainly represents:
options: A memory of earlier time steps
questions.explanation: h_t summarises everything seen so far.

questions.question: RNNs are the natural choice for:
Which architecture was designed specifically for long-term dependencies?
questions.explanation: Gates + cell state counter vanishing gradients.

questions.question: In an encoder–decoder translation model, the encoder:
options: Compresses the input sequence into a context representation
questions.explanation: The decoder then generates from that context.

questions.question: Compared with greedy search, beam search improves:
options: Quality of the generated sequence, by keeping several candidates
questions.explanation: It explores multiple partial outputs instead of committing to one token at a time.

questions.question: The BLEU score measures:
options: How similar a machine translation is to reference translations
questions.explanation: n-gram precision overlap with references, plus a brevity penalty.

questions.question: Why are word embeddings preferred over one-hot vectors?
options: They capture semantic similarity between words
questions.explanation: One-hot vectors are all orthogonal; embeddings place similar words close.

questions.question: Turning "running" into "run" is done by:
questions.explanation: Both reduce words to a base form.

questions.question: In NLP, the "vocabulary" is:
options: The set of all possible labels
The collection of unique tokens the model uses
A list of stop words only
questions.explanation: Every token the model can represent.
